items.body: San Jacinto, up in the Montes de María on Colombia’s Caribbean side, had a dancer called Magdalena Ruiz. The gaiteros remembered her white smile and the grace in the way she moved, and how a gathering lifted the moment she arrived: the musicians, the dancers, the drinking, the young and the old. Adolfo Pacheco remembered her too: “Si no llegaba Magdalena, se enfriaba de la gaita el son”. If she failed to arrive, the gaitas went cold. “Ahora la evoco en mi cantar”, he sings, now I call her up in my song. Those gatherings take the shape of a rueda de cumbia. The musicians stand in the middle and the women dance around them, candles in hand, long skirts sweeping the ground. Caja and gaita set the pace and the circle follows. When Magdalena arrived, that circle opened for her. “Magdalena Ruiz” opens Madre Cumbia, the album Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto, Fruko and Carmelo Torres release on 20 October through the San Diego label Bad Vibes Good Friends. Ten songs, most of them from the sabanera repertoire: three by Andrés Landero, one Torres wrote himself, the rest from writers like Rafael Pérez and Betty Ochoa. Los Gaiteros have carried the gaitas of San Jacinto since the 1940s. Fruko was the bassist and producer who ran the golden era of Discos Fuentes. Carmelo Torres took the accordion straight from Andrés Landero, his teacher and the man who made cumbia sabanera. Between them they hold most of what happened to cumbia in the last eighty years, and this is the first time the three of them have been in a studio together. They recorded in Bogotá with nine musicians in the room, Rory Morison producing and Gabriel Torregrosa directing. On “Magdalena Ruiz” the melody belongs to Iván Salcedo‘s gaita corta, the short flute a San Jacinto cumbia is built on, and Carmelo Torres answers on accordion while Fruko holds the bass underneath. Behind them, caja, conga, guacharaca and maracas keep the rueda turning, and Rafael Castro sings the lead. Listen to “Magdalena Ruiz” and pre-order Madre Cumbia HERE The post Daily Discovery: Los Gaiteros de San Jacinto x Carmelo Torres x Fruko y Sus Tesos – Magdalena Ruiz appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Breton producer Quinquis (Emilie Quinquis) has announced “scenes d’interieur”, her original soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name. The five-track release comes out on 13 November 2026 via Mute. The multi-media production blends theatre and film as it follows Chloe, an actress preparing to perform the role of Nora in Henrik Ibsen’s “A Doll’s House.” The stage sections trace the breakdown of Chloe’s own relationship, while a parallel story shown on film covers her childhood, raised by a mother who survived domestic violence. Ibsen’s 1879 play, which caused a scandal on release for questioning the traditional roles of men and women in marriage, runs through both timelines, tying the production to themes of control and the search for emancipation. Quinquis’ score follows the two timelines, underscoring Chloe’s vulnerability, pain and strength as she navigates the violence of her stepfather as a teenager and of her husband as an adult in the present day. She uses modular electronics to score the live theatre performances and acoustic instrumentation for the film sections, extending the dialogue between past and present that runs through the production. The single “Lena” is an intimate piece where slow-moving synths give way to distant voices as the track builds through layers of emotion. The album was recorded on Ushant Island, off the coast of Brittany, where Quinquis lives, and features a track recorded with Amsterdam-based labelmate Desire Marea, “Inkanuko.” “scenes d’interieur” (catalogue number iMUTE703) carries five tracks: “Chloe,” “Nora,” “Puzuilhan,” “Inkanuko” and “Lena.” It follows Quinquis’ 2025 album “eor” and the 2024 single “Morwreg”, both also released via Mute. About Quinquis Quinquis is the project of Breton producer Emilie Quinquis, based on Ushant Island off the coast of Brittany. Her work moves between electronic and acoustic instrumentation, built around modular synthesis, field recording and a close relationship to the Breton coast where she lives. Quinquis released the “aer” EP and the album “SEIM” before “Morwreg” preceded her 2025 album “eor,” both issued via Mute. “scenes d’interieur,” her soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name, follows in November 2026 and marks her first release built specifically for a theatre production, combining her modular electronic work for the live stage sections with acoustic instrumentation for the production’s film sequences.

items._cn_summary: 布列塔尼制作人Quinquis为舞台剧《Scenes D'interieur》创作原声带，五首作品以模块化电子为核心，辅以原声乐器录制于法国Ushant岛。舞台部分使用模块合成器渲染现场表演，影像段落则采用原声编制，形成过去与现在的声学对话。专辑围绕演员Chloe准备出演易卜生《玩偶之家》中Nora角色的过程展开，两条时间线——少女时期与成年婚姻——交织呈现家庭暴力与女性自我觉醒的主题。曲目“Lena”以缓慢移动的合成器铺底，远处人声渐次浮出，层次堆叠构建情绪张力；“Inkanuko”则与阿姆斯特丹厂牌同僚Desire Marea合作完成。该项目是Quinquis首部专为剧场制作构建的作品，延续其2025年专辑《eor》的电子声响实验方向，厂牌Mute虽具一定知名度但在独立实验领域享有声誉。整体在电子氛围、剧场音乐与世界音乐元素之间寻求融合。

items.body: 東京都交響楽団第1049回定期演奏会Aシリーズ Tokyo Metropolitan Symphony Orchestra Subscription Concert No.1049 A Series 2026年8月8日 東京芸術劇場 2026/8/8 Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre Reviewed by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) Photos by (c)Rikimaru Hotta／提供：東京都交響楽団 <演奏> 指揮：尾高忠明 ピアノ：北村朋幹(*) コンサートマスター：山本友重 東京都交響楽団 <曲目> 三善晃：オーケストラのための『ノエシス』 松村禎三：『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』(*) エルガー：『エニグマ変奏曲』   “無”と書いた軸を掛けても、何もなくなりません。“死”と書いた軸の場合は、何もかもなくなる。“無”ではなくならん。“死”ではなくなる！ 井上靖『本覺坊遺文』より 本公演の前半2曲、三善晃『ノエシス』と松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』に深く刻み込まれているのは、人間がそこから逃れることのできない「死」という事象であった。 6分ほどのごく短い作品ながら、三善の音楽の全ての要素が含まれていると言っても過言ではない『ノエシス』の、雷神か怨霊が乱れ狂い歌い狂うような音響に続く後奏の静けさ。その静けさを構成するのは、「死」だ。いや、乱れ歌う音響もまた「死」の体験を延長したものなのかもしれない。なんと苛烈な世界で三善は生きてきたのか。苛烈な世界で「死」を忘れることなく想いつつ、生き抜いた彼の美的倫理……ああ、過酷だ。あまりにも過酷すぎる。 松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』、これもまた苛烈な音楽であった。松村の原体験に結核での長い療養生活があることは周知の事実だが、その生と死が紙一重となった体験を「凝視すること」を音楽体験に変換した「オスティナート（執拗な反復）」の楽想の恐ろしさ。師・伊福部昭の、生を肯定するたくましいオスティナートとは全く異なる、ひたすら「死とは何か」を念じ続ける強迫的なオスティナート。第1楽章序盤から結末まで、北村朋幹の澄み切ったピアノの音色が音楽に透徹した思索性を与え、またそのピアノを起点としてのオーケストラの響きを捌き切る尾高の指揮、それに応える都響の演奏、どこにも隙がない。隙がないということは松村オスティナートの強迫的音響が終始こちらの心の芯に刺さり、震わせ続けるということだ。なんたる音楽体験。 第2楽章に入り、冒頭からの静かな北村のピアノ独奏が厳しく、されど儚く、でも死を凝視する強い意志をもって。諸行無常という諦観とは無縁な、もっと力強い音楽。やがて始まるピアノのトレモロに生命力が宿り、そこからオーケストラとピアノの強靭な楽想が噴火する。これは生への意志か？ 死への意志か？ 全てをねじ伏せるような力強さ。だが最後（最期）は静寂の中へ、死へと落ちゆく。全てはそこに帰す、という厳然たる真実をこちらに突きつけて、終わる。 公演後半は、人類が2つの世界大戦を経験する以前のいわゆる「クラシック音楽」であるエルガー『エニグマ変奏曲』の美しさを、エルガーの世界的権威尾高忠明の指揮で聴くというなんとも贅沢なプログラムであった。 最初に憂いを帯びた主題が提示される時点で「あー、クラシック音楽は綺麗だ」とうっとりとさせられる。そこから典雅な第1変奏、無窮動的第2変奏、おどけた第3変奏……と進むそれぞれの音楽が実に「これでしかありえない」という確固たる構築性を持って組み立てられている。ヨーロッパの教会建築のような堂々たる荘厳かつ崇高な音楽が現前し、そこに筆者は音楽の持つ陽性な宗教的精神すら汲み取った。さらに、建築といってもガチガチに表面なや内部が固まることなく、生物的な柔軟さとしなやかさをも兼ね備えた有機的建築物である。第9変奏「ニムロッド」の優しく温かい音楽や、最終第14変奏の即興的ダイナミズムを持ちつつ完璧な構造を現実化したレアリゼなど、まさに尾高の独壇場ではないか。なんというか、「さすが世界レベルの権威だ」とぐうの音も出ないほどに心服させられた。 死を強く思わせる前半、優しく抱きしめてくれる後半、と対照的な音楽ながら、どちらも超一流の仕事を聴かせてもらった。尾高マエストロ、北村朋幹、都響、皆に心からの賛辞を。 (2026/9/15)
items._cn_summary: 本乐评记录东京交响乐团第1049回定期演奏会，上半场聚焦日本当代作曲家三善晃《诺埃西斯》与松村禎三《第二钢琴协奏曲》，下半场为埃尔加《谜语变奏曲》。三善作品以雷神般狂暴音响与死寂后奏构成强烈对比，松村协奏曲则将结核療養经历中的生死体验转化为执拗反復的强迫性音响，北村朋幹钢琴音色澄澈，尾高忠明指挥与都響配合严密无隙。下半场埃尔加作品在权威诠释下展现出欧洲教堂般的有机建筑感。整篇乐评以「死」为核心命题串联前后半场，体现了对当代日本严肃音乐深层精神性的哲思性解读。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了Alison Cotton一贯的模糊边界风格，将民谣、前卫元素与宗教感氛围融合。乐器以中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心，加入鼓、贝斯和合成器扩展层次。多数曲目为即兴演奏，一遍成型，营造出穿越时空的静谧神秘气质。专辑是Cotton对2024年末去世父亲的悼念之作，多首曲目流露出深沉的失落感，尤其是描绘父亲最后一次造访他所钟爱的小菜园之作《The Final Harvest》，充满难以言喻的温柔。整张专辑明暗交织，情绪流转，既挑战听者又带来满足与感动，音乐超越类型标签，作为Cotton的作品本身就足以定义其价值。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了贝宁作曲家Antoine Dougbét与Orchestre Poly-Rythmo于1977至1982年间的合作作品，根植于伏都教传统的Sato与Sakpata节奏体系。Dougbé以拍击大腿制造Cavacha节奏闻名，这一律动由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏发展而来，后广泛影响1970年代中期的刚果流行音乐。专辑融合了古巴son的旋律特征与刚果伦巴的律动，同时展现了80年代初合成器进入非洲流行音乐后产生的塑料质感和音色变化。吉他高亮闪烁，踩镲节奏密集，合成器铺底形成层次，作品虽录制年代短暂，仅三张专辑和数支单曲，但密度和力度俱佳。Analog Africa作为专注于非洲冷门音乐的独立厂牌，持续挖掘此类被忽视的非洲流行音乐档案，此辑为该系列第四十四号发行。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur乐队录制，灵感源自1986年他与地下漫画家Robert Crumb的相遇。专辑收录27首短曲，以手风琴为核心，融合法国bal-musette、拉格泰姆、班卓琴音乐、法国香颂与skiffle等多种风格，演奏乐器包括手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风琴及音乐锯等。Cravic以近似日常絮语的方式演唱，带有Maurice Chevalier的影子。专辑既包含向已故法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的严肃曲目，也收录1925年经典曲目《Ukulele Lady》等幽默作品。整体呈现为对被遗忘音乐风格的重新发掘与活化，由一群七旬上下的音乐人以热情与严谨的态度完成。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣界资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统音乐为主，成员各自带来不同的音乐视角。整体弥漫着古老而粗粝的氛围：开场曲以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；唯一的原创曲目引入口簧琴和风笛形成强劲推动力；传统曲目中铙钹琴增添细腻底色，口簧琴与长笛、弦乐交织的器乐曲展现出令人兴奋的失衡感。这是一张展现乐队成熟度的引介之作，五首曲目已显老练，但作为EP篇幅有限，后续发展值得关注。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / soundscape
items._cn_summary: 这是一张在芝加哥南区录制的田野录音作品，并非传统意义上的音乐专辑。录音师Ian Brennan在枪支暴力频发的社区街头，邀请二十五位枪支暴力幸存者即兴讲述自身经历，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。作品无任何配乐添加，所有声音均来自现场环境，包括蚊子、飞机降落声、街头杂音等。一位失去两个儿子的年长女性在讲述中情绪崩溃，反复道歉，而这正是社会结构性暴力最直接的证词。录制当天恰好是特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队的日子。录音全部利润将捐赠给Cure Violence Global。从风格上看，这更接近声音艺术与田野录音的结合，介于实验音乐与社会纪实之间，编辑选择直接呈现录音师评论与原始素材，放弃了传统乐评框架。

items._genre: experimental jazz / free improvisation / contemporary composition
items._cn_summary: 加拿大作曲家、萨克斯手及即兴演奏者 Nicola Miller 与 Frank Gratkowski、Nick Fraser 合作，在专辑《SPIT!》中探索了一套系统化的作曲方法。她运用频谱分析技术将录音中的语音转化为具体音高与四分之一音和声体系，将语言学结构映射到声音频谱层面。此外，部分曲目采用了某种随机语言处理流程，将文字生成的随机性引入音乐结构。三位演奏者在 Watch That Ends the Night 厂牌的合作呈现出学院派爵士与当代作曲技法交汇的特征，乐器即兴段落与谱面创作之间形成对照。由于原文为访谈预告摘录，信息有限，无法充分评估专辑实际音响效果与整体结构，但从方法论描述来看，该作品体现了对声音来源转化与微观音程关系的持续关注，适合对作曲过程感兴趣且熟悉当代即兴语境的听众。

items.body: In this latest instalment of the Secret History of Film Music, Philip Brophy considers how Jon Brion’s music engenders sympathy for the flawed characters in Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another (2025) and Punch-Drunk Love (2002), and Greta Gerwig’s Lady Bird (2017). As discussed in the previous essay in this series, Jonny Greenwood provides an amazing score for Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another (2025). But two pieces by an earlier composer of Anderson’s films bookend the movie: Jon Brion’s “Bunker Bumper” and “Global Bully”. In One Battle After Another, they function as quietly majestic statements of the drive and exhaustion which propel the intergenerational tale of social reparation and familial separation. “Bunker Bumper” uncoils as a disjointed bossa nova: a gently struck bass drum marks time for the snare, hi-hats and cymbals, skipping with a detached, dainty air. Horns and strings entwine like a billowing flag in slow motion. Sometimes the horns are silenced as the strings climb high, as if they’re searching for something. The music feels absent of harmonic progression; it simply surges, even struggles ahead. It plays near the opening as Pat (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Perfidia (Teyana Taylor) and their radical group French 75 attack a border internment camp. The music intones a sad, fatalistic comment on the limited impact of such revolutionary zeal despite the commitment of its participants. The second track “Global Bully” plays at the film’s end. Years later, Pat relaxes at home with his young adult daughter Willa (Chase Infiniti), offspring of Pat and the long absent Perfidia. The domestic scene shows Willa reading a letter from her mother. In a voiceover, Perfidia acknowledges her mistake in deserting Willa, and expresses hope they will one day meet again. Over a lilting percussive pattern, more strings and horns are orchestrated, but here they coalesce around a chordal pattern. The drums call to mind the tinklers of North American tribal shell shakers engaged in ceremonial dances; the orchestra feels like a calming eulogy played at a church service. The piece acquiesces to how the feisty past can dissolve into a depleted present. It concludes with a touching embrace between Pat and Willa. To label the placement of “Global Bully” here as mere closure misses the weight and precision that Brion’s music bestows on the scene. Across Anderson’s first four films, Brion developed a unique modus operandi of embedding music into movies which, arguably, redefined standard operations of ‘scoring’ and ‘accompaniment’. These two Brion tracks in One Battle After Another were recorded and produced 23 years earlier, for Anderson’s Punch-Drunk Love (2002). That film’s sessions saw Brion continually feeding Anderson with ideas, sketches, recordings and even multitrack breakdowns. All were offered not as thorny strictures, but as flexible flotsam to be experimented with, in terms of how their sono-musical character could enhance and shape onscreen characters. How apt that some of these unused tracks surfaced decades later. As Brion has said: “There are lots of [film composers] doing great things, but it comes down to the director’s ‘follow-through’.” A small suite of prepared piano and percussion ensemble pieces makes up a sizable part of the Punch-Drunk Love score. They sound jittery and clackety, like a wooden digestive system attempting to process parts of a drum kit. They initially read as sound effects more than music – a perceptual doubting, enabled by Gary Rydstrom’s deft mix which folds Brion’s trap kit into Christopher Scarabosio’s sound design (who has handled every Paul Thomas Anderson film since). “Le Petit Chateau” and “Hands And Feet” were based on micro-cassette recordings Brion made of Anderson verbally articulating his ideas for rhythms he wanted to use as timing devices for the film’s long tracking shots. The voice of Anderson became the hands of Brion which became the limbs of Barry (Adam Sandler) who discombobulates throughout the movie in arabesques of anxiety. Upon its release, many assumed the film to be a comedy, thanks to Sandler, but the point was there for an attuned audience: mentally unstable people often appear ‘ridiculous’, but to laugh at their pained performance is inhumane, not to mention imperceptive. Brion’s music plays two roles here. The first, through its percussive moments, is to sonorise the synaptic hell of Barry’s panic attacks, and how desperately out of sync he is with his own body and those around him. The second lies in the sumptuous waltzes (“Punch-Drunk Melody”, “Third Floor Hallway”, “Blossoms & Blood”) which spread the wondrous hope Barry glimpses when he falls in love with Lena (Emily Watson). Irrespective of cliche, the luscious orchestral arrangements welcome the couple into a better, dreamier world. Brion’s music is key in distinguishing Punch-Drunk Love from early 2000s romcom saturation. His arrangements are subtly saccharine, influenced by the lush strings found in rock and pop ballads circa the 1970s, arranged by Van Dyke Parks, Jack Nitzsche and Paul Buckmaster. Their sonority affectionately referenced the easy listening sparkle of 1950/60s hi-fi arrangements by Nelson Riddle and Les Baxter, through to Percy Faith and Paul Mauriat. Brion’s encyclopaedic embrace of recorded popular music is felt in his distinctive melodic sensibility: a transatlantic nexus of solo-Beatles songcraft and Laurel Canyon recording. To be clear, the recording studio rules here, not the concert hall. Punch-Drunk Love used vintage microphones for many of its sessions. The film score brims with detail, space and clarity. Following Punch-Drunk Love, non-mainstream cinema forged a strange meld of nerdy empathy, hipster cynicism and feminist angles in ‘relationship dramedies’: David O Russell’s I Heart Huckabees (2004); Charlie Kaufman’s Eternal Sunshine Of The Spotless Mind (2004) and Synecdoche, New York (2008); Miranda July’s The Future (2011); Judd Apatow’s This Is 40 (2012) and Trainwreck (2015); and Greta Gerwig’s Lady Bird (2017). These films cannily merged po-faced ridicule with heartfelt feeling, to varying degrees of success. Yet in all these titles, Brion’s music fortifies their narratives with an endearing romantic sensibility earned by their dysfunctional, antisocial and ‘spectrum’ characters. His Canyon-esque saunter and rich instrumental layering ameliorates any dismissive urges the films’ characters elicit. In Lady Bird, the titular lead (Saoirse Ronan) feels intentionally unlikeable. Equally deliberate is how Brion’s score waltzes around Lady Bird’s teen sense of independence. The film concludes with Lady Bird finally on her own, enrolled in a New York college. At a public phone, she leaves a message for her mother, admitting the rupturing effects of her teen angst created a wedge between them. Brion performs the resonant piano theme like a silent movie accompanist: trilling high notes and copying what’s happening on screen while allowing it space. Eternal Sunshine Of The Spotless Mind features similar piano themes played over scenes with onscreen dialogue mixed low. This isn’t simply a formal sonic device: it displaces the viewer/auditor from the psychic space of the story – where you identify or read what’s happening to characters on screen – and relocates you within the characters’ headspace. Positioned this way, the audience can feel a touch exposed, implicated in being present when characters are at their most vulnerable. “Global Bully” fades up in One Battle After Another as we see Lockjaw (Sean Penn) gassed and hear Pat prepare Willa for Perfidia’s letter: death and life fused through emotive exhalation. That seems to be a throughline in the work Brion has provided across the film and music industries. In discussions with Anderson, Brion noted the aim of Punch-Drunk Love was to “feel like a musical, but nobody ever breaks into song”. Brion’s music – and his tremulous voice which has appeared in songs in many of the films mentioned – is similarly shaped by repression, tension and elation, in a fountain of emotional surges. Musical theatre sceptics mostly react against the unbridled emotionalism of onscreen characters liberated from their realistic surroundings. Yet this transcendental effect functions perfectly in recorded songs and popular music in general, generating one of music’s prime private pleasures. Brion and his collaborators have long embraced how song sonics skilfully embedded in the production of a film score can be exhilaratingly transgressive. Wire subscribers can read Philip Brophy’s original Secret History of Film Music columns from the 1990s online in the digital archive. It was revived in 2025 as an online column: previous instalments published on The Wire website can be read here. Wire readers and print and digital subscribers can also find this essay on page 16 of The Wire 512.

items._cn_summary: 本文探讨Jon Brion为Paul Thomas Anderson电影创作的两首曲目——'Bunker Bumper'与'Global Bully'，它们最初录制于2002年《Punch-Drunk Love》时期，却在2025年新作《One Battle After Another》中被重新运用，形成跨越二十三年的音乐呼应。文章详细分析了两首作品的编排与功能：前者以散拍波萨诺瓦为基底，低音鼓与钹声营造疏离感，弦乐与铜管交织如慢动作中的旗帜飘扬；后者则通过打击乐模式与和声结构形成类似部落仪式与教堂悼词的氛围。文中指出Brion的创作方法模糊了配乐与伴奏的传统边界，将音乐嵌入叙事结构而非简单烘托画面。整体评论聚焦于电影音乐的功能性与情感表达，涉及管弦乐编排与流行元素的混合，但与实验前卫或即兴音乐领域关联较弱。

items.body: Sebastian R. Komor has launched a new project, SRK Group, with the single “Spitfire”, released September 11, 2026 on Infacted Recordings. The Polish-born, Norwegian-raised, Canada-based producer is best known as a longtime member of Icon of Coil. “Spitfire” combines dark electro, EBM and club-oriented electronics. Komor wrote, mixed and produced the track himself at his Xenomorph Productions studio; mastering is also credited to Xenomorph Productions. Describing the song, Komor calls it “personal, loud and danceable.” Spitfire by SRK Group “Spitfire” is available now on Bandcamp and streaming services. About Sebastian Komor Sebastian R. Komor was born in Zabrze, Poland, on May 7, 1976, and moved to Norway in 1981, where he grew up in Fredrikstad’s EBM and industrial scene alongside acts such as Apoptygma Berzerk. He released his first demo in 1992 and recorded under names including Melt, Area51, Sector9 and Moonitor before teaming up with fellow Fredrikstad musician Andy LaPlegua. That collaboration led to the formation of Icon of Coil in 1997; Komor became a full member during the production of the debut single “Shallow Nation” in 2000 and went on to co-write the albums “Serenity Is the Devil” (2000), “The Soul Is in the Software” (2002) and “Machines Are Us” (2004). Komor relocated to Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, in 2004. The following year he started Zombie Girl with Renee Cooper, releasing an EP in 2006 and the album “Back From the Dead” on Alfa Matrix and Metropolis Records in 2007. He later signed to FiXT for the solo hard techno and industrial project Squarehead, released the techno/tribal album “To the Past From the Future in the Present” as Moonitor, and continued his dark techno and EBM alias Komor Kommando, whose releases include the “One By One” EP on Alfa Matrix in 2022. Beyond his own projects, Komor built an extensive catalogue as a producer, mixer and mastering engineer, working with artists including Apoptygma Berzerk, Front Line Assembly, Ayria, Covenant, Circle of Dust and The True Union. His project Bruderschaft brought him together with Ronan Harris of VNV Nation, Joakim Montelius of Covenant, and Stephan Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk. SRK Group, launched with “Spitfire” on Infacted Recordings, is his newest outlet after roughly three decades in the electronic underground.

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章实质是一篇新闻稿，介绍Sebastian R. Komor以SRK Group名义推出的单曲《Spitfire》。文中并未对音乐本身进行实质性评论，而是大量篇幅介绍其履历背景——波兰出生、挪威成长、现居加拿大，作为Icon of Coil成员的经历，以及他三十年间在EBM和工业场景中的多个项目分支（如Zombie Girl、Komor Kommando、Bruderschaft等）。作品由他在Xenomorph Productions工作室独立完成词作、混音、制作与母带处理，定位为暗电子、EBM与俱乐部取向的结合，Komor本人将其形容为"个人化、响亮且适合跳舞"。对于关注暗潮和工业音乐场景的听众而言，Komor的行业背景具有参考价值，但文章缺乏对声音设计、编曲结构或制作水准的具体评述，信息层面偏向宣传而非乐评。

items.body: Soft Vein All We’ve Known of Heaven Artoffact Records If you’ve been following Los Angeles’ Soft Vein since their first LP in 2023 but hadn’t heard any of the pre-release singles for new album All We’ve Known of Heaven you might be forgiven for wondering if it’s even the same project. It’s not that Justin Chamberlain has entirely changed his approach to music: you’re still getting a lot of the same melancholic melodies of the project’s debut and sophomore records, but with the hyper-gloomy and often dour mood of those albums replaced with a powerful, hopeful yearning. Coupled with Chamberlain’s rapid growth as a songwriter, All We’ve Known of Heaven has emerged as one of year’s most moving and engaging listens. Chamberlain’s biggest asset in both his songcraft and his performances is his sense of restraint. The album’s feeling of intimacy comes directly from how simultaneously laidback and vulnerable it comes across; a cut like “Forgetting You” works because its clean, Knopfler-esque guitar and multi-tracked vocals bring you in, setting you up for the big drum machine claps and a damnably catchy chorus. The effect is that it feels like the songs being sung to you as a listener, not at you. When Chamberlain asks “Is this all we are?/All we know?” on the jaw-dropping synthpop gem “All We’ve Known of Heaven” it’s a question directed at the world at large, its ruminations on the sad state of things in the early days of the 21st century building to a plea for a kinder, more loving world. It’s stirring by virtue of the honesty with which it’s delivered, both vocally and musically, from its tasteful synthwork and the smooth closing saxophone solo, to the cathartic introspection of its lyrics and Chamberlain’s deeply heartfelt vocals. The warmth and passion of the songs are fully supported by the wonderfully lush and refined production from Chamberlain himself, assisted by live member Andrea Mantione of Nuovo Testamento. “Learning to Talk” is a sweet love song about the sense of discovery in being with another person, its little synth and guitar trills and half-whispered opening verse building momentum gradually, the space around the instruments growing into a powerful climax. In one of the record’s best moments on “Chekhov”, the edge of bitterness and disappointment in Chamberlain’s voice is perfectly matched by the ghostly pads that hang behind him like a reminder, suggesting a soft but everpresent ache. Similarly, the Cocteau Twins guitars that adorn “White Towers (White Shores)” work so well because the song’s programmed drums and keys are locked in beneath them, lifting the song up while also pushing it forwards. All We’ve Known of Heaven is comforting, quietly confident, unhurried, and above all an incredibly lovely record to just sit and listen to. Justin Chamberlain’s willingness to let the songs speak for themselves is certainly a part of it; while no doubt there’s passion and investment in every moment of the LP, it’s all presented with an unpretentious and open candor that makes it easy to get swept up in its grand swells of emotion. An absolute stunner of a album, and one of the year’s best to date. Recommended. Buy it. items._cn_summary: Soft Vein 的第二张专辑延续了首作忧郁旋律的核心，却在情绪底色上发生了根本转向——从阴郁沉滞转为充满希望的渴望。Chamberlain 的创作克制而私密，干净的吉他与人声层叠邀请听众进入歌曲内部。《Forgetting You》以克诺普弗风格的吉他配合鼓机拍手，构造出感染力极强的副歌；同名曲以合成器流行为骨架，结尾萨克斯独白为歌曲带来温暖的余韵。《Learning to Talk》通过器乐留白逐步积蓄张力，在安静的合成器颤音中走向高潮。《Chekhov》里幽灵般的音垫与人声中的苦涩边缘形成微妙共振；《White Towers (White Shores)》的回响吉他则让人联想到 Cocteau Twins。专辑整体制作精良而内敛，是一张适合静坐聆听的、情感真挚的合成器流行作品。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — A different step in direction for the band after a few line up changes and a period of inactivity, the band came back with a completely different vibe, but with familiar technical speeds and playing. The attempt at moving into a more progressive sound that they tried on Scruillous is more fully felt on this album, with vocalist Rody Walker almost sounding like a different singer, with a cleaner and less punky sound to his voice. At times his range does show some weakness, but the overall passion on this album from him and the rest of the band is very potent. Lyrically being a concept album based on American exceptionalism, it is very well crafted. The track I'd recommend is From The Sky.

items._cn_summary: 这是Protest the Hero在阵容变动和沉寂期后的回归之作，整体气质发生了明显转向。乐队在前作Scurrilous中尝试的前卫化方向在这张专辑里得到了更充分的展开，主唱Rody Walker的声线变得更为干净、减少了朋克式的粗粝感，虽然音域偶尔显出疲态，但情感浓度依然充沛。器乐层面延续了乐队招牌的技术性高速演奏与复杂编排，技术功底扎实。歌词方面作为一张概念专辑，围绕美国例外论主题展开，文本构建颇为用心。推荐曲目为From The Sky。这张专辑在保持技术金属骨架的同时向前卫领域更深入地推进，属于乐队自身脉络内的一次有意识转向，但与更为实验性、前沿性的前卫音乐相比仍偏向传统技术金属框架。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Last Knight is a musical project established in 1997 by Jose Medina, featuring musicians such as Marc Atkinson (Riversea, Moon Halo), Mariano Gardella, Deibys Artigas, Rafael Pacha (guitars, also with The Samurai of Prog), and Troy Donockley (Nightwish)."The Grand Overture" is a cinematic musical narrative blending classical, folk, and medieval elements?a monumental opening piece with interwoven textures. "In the Middle Ages" navigates between Alan Parsons and the Beatles, featuring a captivating melody sung theatrically by Mariano, accompanied by Sacha's poignant, arpeggiated guitar work that evokes a harsh era. "The Kingdom of Asturias" is an acoustic instrumental reflecting rugged times, with a recorder ushering the listener into a Christian kingdom on the defensive. "A War of Eight Centuries" is an anthemic, chilling interlude with Marc narrating eight centuries of conflict. "Cordoba" features Sacha's arpeggios?recalling a time when beauty and art contended with war?and vibrant Andalusian guitar. On "War," Deibys sings a tune reminiscent of Rainbow, while vintage keyboards evoke Ayreon; Nelson delivers an 80s-style guitar solo that captures the chaos. "Chivalry Tales" is an interlude driven by percussive bass and Hammond organ, with piano flourishes that skip along like knights in battle. "A Green Field of Memories" is a somber ballad, a medieval-style piece humming with acoustic notes."The Kingdom of Leon" serves as a symphonic instrumental sequel?a sweeping epic in the vein of The Samurai of Prog and Alan Parsons. It features spellbinding keyboards, Troy's bagpipes, violins, and various flutes that conjure up the world of *Lord of the Rings*, elves, and imagined medieval tales. The organ engages in a playful duel with the guitar, while the drums drive the entertaining progressive soundscape; a notable mid-song break sees the bass aggressively challenge the organ in a moment that feels simultaneously Floyd-esque, Western, and cinematic. Note the finale, where the Andalusian influence revisits the "Spaghetti Western" atmosphere to create something truly divine. "Flames Would Rise"?referencing the flames meant for heretics?features a scorching vocal performance that sends shivers down the spine. "Across the Mountains" serves as an interlude that traverses the Pyrenees on the wings of a flute melody. "The Kingdom of Galicia" offers a second epic tableau, blending folk, jazz, and world music vibes; it features a hushed, atmospheric sound reminiscent of Unitopia, balanced by Oldfield-esque Celtic moods and hurdy-gurdy and mandolin played by Sacha. There is room for furious heavy guitar work and a cinematic melting pot narrated by Mariano, acting as the resident bard. Mellotron adds a sentimental medieval touch, leading into a distinctive outro. "Pamplona" is a baroque harpsichord interlude that captures an elegiac splendor. "The Backyard" is a pastoral sketch for flute and acoustic guitar, paving the way for a cinematic finale. Finally, "Hymn for Asturias" features Deibys singing of the cycle's end?a prayerful lament that nonetheless exudes hope, underscored by Troy's flute.Last Knight?a tale of medieval glory; rest assured, this first saga will captivate you, marking the beginning of a trilogy. It is a concept of cathedral-like proportions, blending symphonic prog with exhilarating cinematic folk. A perfect example of the genre.
items._genre: crossover prog / symphonic prog / folk prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以中世纪西班牙收复失地运动为叙事框架，通过大量器乐短曲与史诗段落交替推进。古典、民间与中世纪元素交织，吉他、键盘、风笛、竖琴与曼陀林等乐器构成丰富的声景层次。部分段落尝试融入安达卢西亚风格与爵士元素，但整体仍以叙事为主导，未深入探索前卫实验或非常规声响设计。专辑结构偏向传统前摇叙事逻辑，适合对历史主题感兴趣且偏好器乐丰富的听众。

items.body: Lords Of Acid release “Ich Will Nur Das” (I Just Want) on Metropolis Records on 11 September 2026, the group’s fourth single of the year. The frenetic dance track features a vocal by US electronic musician Mari Kattman, sung entirely in German. Ich Will Nur Das by Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid founder Praga Khan describes the track as “basically a love song with a serious identity crisis. The verses are pure lust: hot, dirty, aggressive and completely unapologetic. Then the chorus suddenly turns into the romantic fantasy of a lovestruck teenager dreaming about eternal love.” Kattman is a Metropolis Records labelmate and a non-German speaker who has been touring on her own recent solo album, “Year Of The Katt.” “She was perfect for this song, as it is incredibly charming to hear her American voice attack these German lyrics,” Khan said. “We didn’t want her pronunciation to be too polished or perfect, as her accent gives the track extra personality. She also understood the contradiction at the heart of the song: one minute she sounds like she wants to devour you, the next she’s dreaming about everlasting love. It’s filthy and innocent at the same time, which is pretty much Lords Of Acid in a nutshell.” “Ich Will Nur Das” follows the previously released “Karaoke Superstar” featuring Princess Superstar, “Dream Boy” featuring Carla Harvey, and “El Mundo Esta Loco” featuring Tony & The Kiki. All four songs appear on “Mundo Bizarro,” the group’s new album, which streams digitally from 15 October to coincide with part two of the “Cheeky Freaky” US tour, with LP and CD editions following on 6 November. “Mundo Bizarro” tracklist: “Dream Boy,” “Dancing On The Flames,” “El Mundo Esta Loco,” “Dopamine War,” “Maximo Roboto,” “Ich Will Nur Das,” “City Of Angels,” “So Stoned Today,” “Karaoke Superstar,” “You’re Obscene” and “A Viking’s Heart.” About Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid formed in Antwerp, Belgium in 1988 around Praga Khan and are recognised as one of the most influential acts to emerge from the hard-edged electronic dance music scene of that era, blending techno, acid house and industrial music with lyrics on sexuality, drug use and hedonism. The group debuted with the New Beat single “I Sit On Acid,” and its debut album “Lust” appeared in 1991, followed by further releases that saw the band become a staple of the Billboard dance and alternative charts. Carla Harvey, formerly of Butcher Babies, joined as singer in 2025. Having built a global following across a multi-decade touring career, Lords Of Acid remain one of the genre’s most recognisable names, with “Ich Will Nur Das” arriving ahead of the group’s next album, “Mundo Bizarro,” streaming digitally from 15 October 2026 ahead of LP and CD editions on 6 November.
items._cn_summary: Lords Of Acid 成立于1988年比利时安特卫普，是硬派电子舞曲领域的重要团体，融合techno、acid house与工业元素，歌词涉及性、药物与享乐主义。新单曲'Ich Will Nur Das'为德语演唱，邀请美国电子音乐人Mari Kattman献声，制作人Praga Khan称其为'带有严重身份危机的情歌'——主歌部分充满欲望与侵略性，副歌却转向少女般的浪漫幻想，不完美的德语发音反而成为特色。该曲收录于新专辑'Mundo Bizarro'，与'Dream Boy''Karaoke Superstar''El Mundo Esta Loco'等共同构成完整曲目。专辑数字版于10月15日发行，实物版11月6日推出，配合美国巡演第二阶段。这是一篇纯新闻稿式发布通告，缺乏深度乐评视角与音乐分析。

items.body: Cold Spring hosts a label night at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, with T.A.G.C., Satori, Colossloth and Llyn Y Cwn performing alongside a Cold Spring stall. Doors run from 7pm to 10:30pm, with tickets available through Resident Advisor and the event’s Facebook page. T.A.G.C. (The Anti Group Communications) was devised by Adi Newton and Steven James Turner in 1978 as a multi-dimensional research and development project. Newton uses T.A.G.C. as an outlet for his research into psycho-acoustic music, built from carefully constructed aural rituals. He is also the driving force behind Clock DVA, The Anti Group and The Future, the pre-Human League project, and a key figure in the development of electronic, industrial and experimental music since the late 1970s. T.A.G.C.’s “Iso-Erotic Calibration” is out now on Cold Spring on CD, LP and limited LP. British industrial veterans Satori formed in 1984 and have released material on cult labels including Broken Flag, Mindscan, Cold Spring and Tesco Organisation. The Glossop date doubles as the launch for Satori’s new album, “Your Life Is Worth Nothing,” which pairs harsh noise and power electronics with heavier percussive beats than the act’s earlier material. Colossloth, from the Midlands, marks 20 years as a project in 2026 and launches the new album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” at the Glossop show. Colossloth’s music moves between brooding, abrasive passages and more transcendental material, drawing on industrial, ethnic tribalism and rave influences. Llyn Y Cwn is the solo project of Ben Powell, who has made electronic music for over 25 years, drawing on the landscapes of North Wales and his experience on Arctic research cruises. He presents “Megaliths In Dub” versus “Aniara” as an exclusive first listen at the Glossop show. About Cold Spring Cold Spring is a British independent record label focused on industrial, power electronics, noise, dark ambient and experimental music. The label has released material from artists including T.A.G.C., Satori and Colossloth, and has previously staged label nights and compilations such as the “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” collection. The Glossop show brings together acts from across the label’s roster, including two new album launches from Satori and Colossloth, alongside a live set from Clock DVA and Human League co-founder Adi Newton under his T.A.G.C. name.
items._genre: industrial / power electronics / experimental / dark ambient / noise

items.body: Band: Mastodon | Album: Marrow Deep | Genre: Progressive metal | Year: 2026 From: Atlanta, USA | Label: Loma Vista Bandcamp Mastodon is a trailblazing band in the realm of modern metal. As it stands, prog-sludge is one of the most popular varieties of progressive metal, at least by the sheer number of bands playing in that style, and much of that popularity can surely be attributed to these Atlantans. In revisiting their discography prior to writing this review, I noticed something of a parallel to Metallica’s career trajectory. Both bands started off with four absolutely stunning albums. This phase of work was then followed by a shift toward more radio-friendly sounds. (Obviously, The Hunter was nowhere near the success that Metallica’s self-titled was, but there are still overarching similarities.) Metallica’s subsequent records have ranged from middling (Death Magnetic, Hardwired), to awful (Reload, St. Anger), to downright baffling (Lulu). Mastodon, meanwhile, has been more consistent (and simply better, to be frank), but their output since the masterpiece that is Crack the Skye has oscillated boring-to-okay. Marrow Deep, the group’s ninth LP, comes at a time of major change for the band. It follows five years after their last album, the perfectly fine but overlong Hushed & Grim. It’s also their first release since the death of guitarist-vocalist Brent Hinds, following his messy firing from the band. Longtime touring keyboardist João Nogueira has also joined the band, officially making Mastodon a quintet, alongside new guitarist Nick Johnston. The album opens with “Barbarians Blood”, where twisting guitar lines lead a stomping rhythm in its opening moments. There are more restrained passages, where guitars skitter about and keyboards add an eerie atmosphere. Additional flavors are drawn from sources as disparate as punk and jazz. Troy Sanders and Brann Dailor trade lead vocals, but this song gels beautifully. “Poisonous Weapons” continues on in a similar vein, with perhaps a more psychedelic atmosphere. I love the integration of keys into Mastodon’s sound. It makes everything feel so lush and rich. Not that they necessarily struggled on that front previously, but it’s an exciting new variation. Contrasts in tempo and intensity continue on “Your Ghost Again”. Brann’s vocals, in particular, soar and feel majestic atop the swirling instrumental backdrop. “Snakes for Dinner” calls back to Mastodon’s earliest releases with its raw energy and powerful groove, while the soaring chorus pulls in their best moments from albums like Once More Round the Sun. The synth solo is a ton of fun, too, and it’s exciting to hear keys play more than a supporting role for this band. “Out Like a Lamb” has a more restrained opening. It’s not a gentle song, but the riffs are more controlled, and the drumming is more tight than propulsive. Keyboard embellishments add some fun texture, and in the moments where the band does let loose, twangy clean guitar notes cut through for some fun, subtle contrast. By its end, this song begins feeling a little long, despite all its good qualities. Clean guitar and tinkling synths provide a mellow and rather pretty opening to “In the Ruins”. Even when the distorted guitar comes in, it’s more scratchy than blistering, lending a certain antique rustiness that fits the title well.That is, at least until guitars like machine guns burst in and the song launches off at a gallop. Despite having a lot of good elements, this song doesn’t quite come together in the same way as the preceding cuts. It’s all solid music, but things here just don’t quite fit together. The opening of “They’re Coming for You” features some of the clearest classic prog influence on the record. Speedy, technical instrumental lines swirl around each other, and the combination of metal with organ and electric piano remind me of some of Opeth’s work. In fact, this is a very Opeth-y song overall, with its gothic-tinged verses and gentle moments of contrast. It’s around this point in the album that things started running together a bit for me. “Golden Spires” is a solid cut, if not exactly distinct in the context of the record. “Moth and Bone” has a lovely gentle intro, with a more typically Mastodon-y second half. And “A Vampire’s Demeanor” is fairly straightforward, featuring some spookier, Opeth-y elements. None of these songs are bad, but they’re not exactly essential, either. Marrow Deep ends on its two longest songs. “The Vanishing” begins as a quiet, restrained composition. Effects-laden vocals, wiry guitars, and enveloping keyboard tones evoke a dreamy atmosphere. The song’s climax is a powerful passage, with passionate screams and blistering guitar. The album then ends with “The Three Fates”. Mastodon incorporates some alt-rock influence on this cut, especially in the vocal melodies. The midsection features narration over an ominous backing, and it’s mostly a success. Narration is tough to pull off well, but the end result here isn’t too distracting. What is distracting, though, is the jazzy instrumental noodling that follows. A bit of indulgence would have been fine, but this particular passage absolutely overstayed its welcome. Once they ditch the jazz, though, the song ends on a strong instrumental jam. Marrow Deep is Mastodon’s best record since Crack the Skye. The riffs are energetic and vital, with a lot of power and urgency behind them. The addition of a keyboardist has brought new depth to their sound, and the compositions are overall quite strong. It’s not a perfect record, mind you. It is longer than it needs to be, and the band could have taken a scalpel to some of the second half. Despite these gripes, I like what I hear, and it’s good to hear Mastodon back in peak form. Score: 80/100
items._cn_summary: 这是Mastodon第九张录音室专辑的乐评，距离上一张专辑五年后发行。乐队经历了主创吉他手兼主唱Brent Hinds去世与离队的重大变动，长期巡演键盘手João Nogueira正式加入，与新吉他手Nick Johnston共同形成五人阵容。专辑延续乐队标志性的前卫金属与sludge风格，吉他riff与键盘融合营造出层次丰富的音色质感，tempo与强度的对比贯穿各曲目。曲目中融入朋克与爵士元素，Troy Sanders与Brann Dailor交替担任主唱，键盘solo成为亮点之一。整体编曲在保留早期作品原始能量的同时，融入了更为流畅的旋律走向与迷幻氛围。

items.body: When I’m looking for peace and tranquillity, I head for the forest, or for the shore, or for any environment that hasn’t been completely dominated and subdued by human invention and industry. Yet when I arrive there, I’m quick to discover that this supposedly tranquil idyll is anything but; instead, it’s a constantly changing world of sound, movement, light, smells, and weather. Strangely, this tumult doesn’t stop me from finding the peace I’m looking for — in fact, it often seems a necessary condition for it. I can take hold of a moment — the colour of a leaf, the smell of damp soil — knowing that its sudden intensity will soon give way to something else, to boredom and to the next unfolding experience. I sometimes come across this apparent paradox in music, too: in order to truly savour a moment (a timbre, a harmonic colour), I have to accept that it’s only a moment (rhythm, structure). This happy contradiction is writ large across Sarah Louise’s new album, the twelfth in a series of solo acoustic guitar recordings from label Vin Du Select Qualitite. Louise gets stunning tones and timbres from her twelve-string guitar (Volume 12, twelve strings, geddit?), but these rich notes and chords are swept up in leaping, tumbling melodic refrains. Each note is perfectly incomplete, looking forwards to the next one to complete it. This is music as a riverine flow, a fast-moving stream sometimes stumbling over itself in its eagerness to hurry on down the hill towards the valley. Repetition is a sort of exuberance in the act of vanishing, a joy most apparent in the glimmering drive of ‘Late April’. Though this vital movement can be heard in every track on the album, it’s by far the only event happening in this densely-woven twelve-string world. The tension and anxiety of ‘Evidence of a Bear’, the sense of being watched by unseen eyes (or smelt by unseen nose), contrasts with the languid floating of ‘Floating Rhododendron’. The dark drama of ‘Scarab’ seems to come to a tragic conclusion, its storytelling replete with dramatic pauses and shifts in register. But it’s to the woods and mountains and streams that the album constantly turns, not by way of mimicry or simple evocation, but more like an aural memory of being there (even though I’ve never been there before — there being, perhaps, the Blue Ridge Mountains near Louise’s home in North Carolina, or maybe some other place that exists only in the music). In its own way, each piece offers fleeting glimpses of an unforgettable landscape, intense yet vaguely-recalled images of sun, mountains, trees: the landscape a river sees on its way down to the valley.   VDSQ Acoustic Series Volume 12 by Sarah Louise   Sarah Louise Vin Du Select Qualitite
items._cn_summary: Sarah Louise以十二弦吉他独奏为核心，在原声民谣框架内探索音色的丰富性与旋律的流动感。专辑收录VDSQ系列的第十二卷，每首曲目都呈现出如河流般的旋律推进，音符之间相互依存、彼此呼应，既有明亮跳跃的旋律段，也有深沉内省的氛围乐章。她通过精湛的指法技巧营造出多层次的音色织体，将吉他的共鸣推至极致。整体概念围绕自然山林展开——蓝岭山脉的溪流、漂浮的杜鹃花、隐藏的熊踪——这些意象并非简单模仿，而是作为听觉记忆的载体被融入音乐结构之中。评论指出作品在丰富音色与流动结构之间取得平衡，传达出一种在变化中寻找宁静的哲学思考。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John于1999年在德国莱茵河畔Loreley露天剧场的演出，乐队编制精简却充满掌控力，钢琴、吉他、贝斯与鼓构成紧密互动。演出以Mardi Gras游行式编排为框架，混合新奥尔良经典与个人代表作：从'Iko Iko'的半唱半吟社区颂歌，到'Qualified'的放克炫技，再到'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'中将巫毒仪式、丛林嘶吼与迷幻吉他独奏融为一体的funknology美学。专辑还纳入'Duke Ellington'的致敬曲目、'Right Place, Wrong Time'等热门单曲以及Earl King的'Big Chief'收尾。整体演出跨越语言与文化障碍，展现新奥尔良音乐传统的独特精神与民俗根基。

items.body: James Johnston picked up a paintbrush while on tour with PJ Harvey ten years ago and never put it down again. This is what the practice has taught him. Words and candid photography by Wesley Doyle Guildford-born James F. Johnston has spent most of his life known as a musician: founder of Gallon Drunk, a former member of Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, Faust, and Big Sexy Noise with Lydia Lunch, he’s played on records by Barry Adamson, Dot Allison and PJ Harvey. The multi-instrumentalist is now... The post James F. Johnston of Gallon Drunk on Painting appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的音乐评论，而是关于Gallon Drunk乐队创始人James F. Johnston从音乐人转型为画家的艺术人生介绍。文章提到他在巡演途中拾起画笔，将消磨时间的方式发展为日常实践乃至主业，展现了一位跨界艺术家的身份转变轨迹。虽然文中提及他与Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds、PJ Harvey、Lydia Lunch等合作经历，暗示了其音乐背景与实验圈层的关联，但文章主体聚焦于绘画创作而非音乐作品本身，缺乏对专辑声音、编曲、制作或音乐创新的具体讨论。对于关注实验音乐、暗潮及跨领域融合的读者而言，此文提供的人物背景信息有一定参考价值，但作为乐评其音乐分析深度明显不足。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The Bardic Depths are back with Peter Jones contributing as a full member (one of my favorite collaborations that he's done). This is their fourth studio album release of this decade. 1. "Islands" (8:37) excellent and fresh feeling music based on NeoProg sound palette and stylings. I really like the construct, feel, and flow of this song though it does lag a bit in places. (18.333/20)2. "Fallen Leaves" (3:03) GENESISian 12-string-with-organ and anachronistic melody lines open this as harmonized vocal "doo-doo-doo" lines become woven within the instrumental weave. As this pattern continues--throughout the entire song--I find myself rather surprised--and delighted. It's a really cool and fairly inventive (if �tude-like) piece. (8.875/10)3. "Arribabok" (4:48) borrowing a lot from George Harrison/The Beatles' Indian-influenced soundscapes (which were later further developed by the likes of Daevid Allen with his GONG and other projects as well as Steve Hillage and even Peter Gabriel and David Torn). I love Gareth Gole's Torn-Hillage-like guitar tone and play in the third minute. The vocal and congestion and crescendo at the end of the third minute reminds me of both Peter Gabriel's world music and Karl Jenkins' ADIEMUS music. Nice sax play by Peter in the fourth minute and then a nice d�nouement and return to the original palette in the final minute. (9.125/10)4. "October Sun" (8:12) More excellent vocal-centric NeoProg music that reminds me of the fine fare of both FISH ON FRIDAY and TONY PATTERSON (as well as Dave Longdon-era BIG BIG TRAIN). Though the song construct and instrumental play is rather simple and sedate, the bass and vocal work is quite excellent. I understand how solid, comforting "bedding" of easy-to-digest music can serve as an excellent foundation for the exploration/expression of more sincere ideas above it--and this does happen in this song's second half--and I understand the talent and skill it takes to render such a "bedding"--so I am not as critical of this habit or tendency as I used to be (always looking for the sophistication and instrumental virtuosity in each song). I actually really appreciate the way the band has constructed and rendered this song. (17.75/20)5. "From Empty Trees" (4:41) an instrumental opening that sounds like something Tony Banks would have done for Genesis (or himself?) back in the breakout period of the band's popularity. Gareth's guitar work in his lead time during the third minute is okay but nothing very innovative--and the ascending four-chord motif that follows feels so much like Tom Johnson's "Uncertain Smile" ending jam from his 1983 The The album, Soul Mining (with that amazing piano solo from Jools Holland). (8.75/10)6. "A View" (6:18) a gorgeous NeoGenesis weave of arpeggiating keyboard and acoustic and electric guitars with solid low end support from well-coordinated bass and drums also sees some excellent synth strings orchestra and old Mellotron threads in the weave as Peter sings with his usual folk-bard-like approach. Nice weave of multiple other guitar and keyboard lines topped off by a nice heavily-reverbed sax solo from Peter in the fourth minute which is then followed by a fine electric guitar solo. Peter's voice and vocal styling is so classic, so powerful, so iconic. It's no wonder he's been the vocalist of so many 21st Century NeoProg classics. (8.875/10)7. "Harder to See" (4:09) a little more sophistication, syncopation, and frequent key changing makes this an interesting tune--especially when attending to Peter's vocal (he's got to be spot on for this one!) Once the pattern of the four chord motif is established (almost Van Morrison "Moondance"-like), the music becomes more familiar and, thus, comfortable. The chorus and follow-up d�nouement and fade out come easily but are not quite the finish one might hope for. (8.875/10)8. "Rewind" (9:21) this one opens up as another acoustic guitar- and piano-dominated weave that incorporates a four-way vocal approach, lead and harmonies, reminding me of MOON SAFARI as well as bands like Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young or even Wobbler and The Beach Boys. Nice instrumental work in the instrumental section from the third minute to the fifth and then again after 4:40 when things switch to a more ambient/atmospheric palette. (Who's playing the flutes?) This is very psychedelic in its pastoral dream-like feel--very similar to some of Steve Hackett's best stuff ("Cinema Show," Wind and Wuthering, and his early solo albums). Interesting that the the rest of the song (and album) plays out with this atmospheric instrumental weave--five minutes of it (not unlike that odd prolonged ending to "Dancing with the Moonlight Knight")! Luckily, it's really nice! The boys are obviously serious students of the masterpieces of prog's Golden Age. (18.5/20)Total Time 49:09The band's NeoProg music has continued to develop, progressing into more sophisticated and original realms of prog--that remind me of both Peter Gabriel and Fish On Fridays. With any lineup that includes prog-savant Peter Jones one cannot help but have high expectations. The problem comes with the frequent disappointments that come with the feelings of "underdeveloped," "not fully-realized" or "falling short" of possible potentialities. B+/4.5 stars; an excellent album of creative, top-notch NeoProg from some of England's most reverential and proficient veterans. Highly recommended--especially if you like the NeoProg sub-genre where it might be considered an essential masterpiece.
items._cn_summary: The Bardic Depths 第四张录音室专辑邀请 Peter Jones 作为正式成员参与，延续了 Crossover Prog 路线。整体音乐以 NeoProg 为基调，融合 Genesis 式的十二弦吉他与管风琴织体、Harrison 风格的印度音乐色彩，以及 Peter Gabriel 世界音乐与 Karl Jenkins 式的声乐堆叠。编曲以人声为核心，注重旋律的舒适感与铺陈，器乐部分相对克制。评论者对各曲目的细致分析涉及 Beatles 印度影响、Gong 与 Steve Hillage 的吉他语汇，以及 Tom Johnson 式钢琴动机，显示专辑在传统前卫摇滚谱系内做有意识的引用与变奏。音乐整体偏向抒情性与可听性，创新性有限，更注重经典元素的重组而非突破。

items.body: Spanish producer Nightcrawler releases the single “Reactor 4” on September 17, 2026, the first track from his forthcoming album “Uranium 235” on Nightcrawler Music. An official video accompanies the release. “Reactor 4” mixes dark techno, industrial electronics and cinematic textures. The single and its video take their titles from nuclear engineering, and Nightcrawler describes the video as the first look into the album’s dystopian universe, setting up “Uranium 235” as a concept record built around that imagery. The track was produced, mixed and mastered at NC Sound Studio, Nightcrawler’s own studio. Nightcrawler also directed the video, and cover design comes from George Gold Design, which also created the artwork for the 2025 Nightcrawler and Spammerheads collaboration “Ghostless”. “Reactor 4” arrives on all digital platforms and Bandcamp from September 17. About Nightcrawler Nightcrawler is a Spanish electronic music project active since 2011, built around horror and sci-fi film scores and a mix of dark atmospheres with driving electronic rhythms. The project released the “Strange Shadows” EP in 2014 and built out an extensive Bandcamp catalogue since, including releases such as “Visionary”, “Metropolis” and the “Corrupted System” and “R.U.S.H.” singles. In April 2025, Nightcrawler teamed up with the Valencia-based EBM duo Spammerheads for the collaborative single “Ghostless”, which Side-Line covered at the time. On November 13, 2025, Nightcrawler released the album “Malevolent Forces” through Nightcrawler Music, an eight-track record built on film-inspired EBM and spoken-word samples that Side-Line reviewed. “Reactor 4”, out September 17, 2026, is the first single from the project’s next album, “Uranium 235”. Nightcrawler continues to release music independently through Nightcrawler Music.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于西班牙电子音乐人 Nightcrawler 新单曲发布的资讯稿，介绍了其新单曲《Reactor 4》及其即将发行的专辑《Uranium 235》的背景信息。整篇文章以新闻发布的形式呈现，包含发行日期、厂牌、制作人员及艺人简介等基本信息，描述中提及作品融合了暗潮科技舞曲、工业电子和电影化音色质感，以核工程为主题构建反乌托邦概念，歌词与视觉均取材于核能意象。Nightcrawler 自有厂牌 Nightcrawler Music 独立发行，混音与母带处理均在其个人工作室完成。整体内容属于标准化的单曲发行通告，缺乏对音乐本身声音设计、编曲结构、节奏处理或情感表达的深入评析，未能提供足够的审美信息来评估作品的艺术价值。
